what_it_proves: Burlington is a scaled physical-store off-price operator.
boundary: Store count proves reach, not store productivity or durable customer loyalty.

what_it_proves: The model is overwhelmingly store-native, not digital-led.
boundary: Store-native sales do not prove traffic quality or cash conversion by themselves.

what_it_proves: The company has a large physical operating footprint.
boundary: Square footage does not prove sales density, margin, or return on new stores.

what_it_proves: The customer-facing store base is large enough to matter nationally.
boundary: Selling space needs productivity, inventory turn, and traffic support to become durable cash.

what_it_proves: The bargain model requires physical distribution capacity.
boundary: Distribution capacity does not prove merchandise quality or margin durability.

what_it_proves: Liquidity and inventory funding capacity are visible.
boundary: ABL size is not a populated borrowing-base certificate or collateral performance proof.

what_it_proves: The company had substantial unused borrowing capacity.
boundary: Unused capacity does not prove inventory eligibility, cash receipts, or return on capital.

what_it_proves: The growth sequence started before the strongest quarters.
boundary: Sales growth does not separate traffic, ticket, new stores, or pricing effects.
A low positive comp does not prove durable consumer demand or merchandise quality.
Momentum can reverse if merchandise availability, traffic, or consumer budgets weaken.
Comp growth does not prove cash quality without margin, inventory turn, shrink, and working-capital support.

what_it_proves: Off-price demand accelerated while the store base expanded.
boundary: One strong quarter does not prove permanent trade-down, store productivity, or inventory-to-cash quality.
